The CIA's Master's in Food Business Management is not just academic it's transformative, preparing you with the expertise and acumen to lead in today's dynamically changing food landscape. title: Leveraging Digital Tools for Enhanced Customer Experience in Independent Restaurants
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: The restaurant industry is undergoing an unprecedented transformation, driven by a myriad of digital advancements. From advanced Point of Sale (POS) systems to Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven inventory management, sm

body.text: A Winning Recipe for Customer Satisfaction

The restaurant industry is undergoing an unprecedented transformation, driven by a myriad of digital advancements. From advanced Point of Sale (POS) systems to Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven inventory management, small to medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in the restaurant space are perfectly positioned to leverage these innovative solutions. However, the sheer volume and complexity of technological options can leave restaurant owners bewildered about which investments will truly offer value.

Savvy independent restaurant operators are integrating cutting-edge technology to streamline operations while preserving their unique character. Customers are seeking seamless digital experiences combined with the personalized touch that defines a memorable dining occasion. By making strategic digital choices, these establishments can deliver on these expectations and thrive in a highly competitive market.
The Independent Restaurant Landscape
Balancing Charm and Challenges

SMBs typically operate with 50 employees or fewer per location. About 9 in 10 restaurants run on this lean staffing model, solidifying their role as the industry's backbone. These establishments range from cherished local diners to emerging regional chains, embodying an entrepreneurial spirit that balances ambition with heartfelt charm, fostering unparalleled customer loyalty.

Nevertheless, these restaurants face significant hurdles. According to the National Restaurant Association, nearly half of restaurant leaders are struggling to meet consumer demand due to understaffing. Additionally, 31% report that recruiting and hiring new employees has become even more challenging in 2024 compared to previous years.

With 70% of consumers agreeing that technology enhances their restaurant experience, demands for convenience-enhancing options such as smartphone accessibility, web-based ordering, and digital payment systems are rising. These preferences add another layer of complexity to restaurant operations.

To overcome these challenges, meet customer expectations, and bridge the labor gap, restaurants are increasingly turning to technology, channeling an average of 7-10% of gross revenue into IT investments.
Core Technologies Reshaping SMBs
Key Areas of Technological Investment
For small-to-medium restaurants, "the right tech" means balancing innovation with practicality in critical operational areas.

Kitchen Tech: Core technologies like smart kitchen equipment and Kitchen Display Systems (KDS) are revolutionizing the industry. For example, programmable ovens and IoT-enabled refrigerators optimize cooking and inventory management. KDS streamline operations by providing essential service metrics and customized workflows. These technologies enhance efficiency, maintain food quality, and reduce operational costs, addressing the sustainability concerns vital to modern customers.

AI Inventory Management: AI-driven inventory management systems eradicate the need for manual stock counts and guesswork, predict usage patterns, automate reordering, and even suggest menu modifications based on ingredient availability. Implementing such solutions can substantially reduce waste, control costs, and ensure that chefs always have the right ingredients at their disposal.

Data Analysis: With the abundance of data available, analytics and business intelligence tools are indispensable for SMBs. With 51% of Americans dining out at least once a week, 43% using apps for takeout multiple times, and 52% participating in loyalty programs, restaurants generate a wealth of data. Forward-thinking operators leverage this information to make informed staffing decisions, develop targeted marketing strategies, and create personalized dining experiences that foster lasting customer loyalty.

Next-Gen Point of Sale Systems: Modern Point of Sale systems do much more than process transactions. Serving as the nucleus of restaurant operations, these systems integrate with various technologies, provide real-time reporting, and offer customer relationship management features. For expanding restaurant chains, robust Point of Sale systems are essential for connecting all aspects of the business and ensuring smooth and cohesive operations.

By strategically implementing these technologies, independent restaurants can effectively address their challenges, from alleviating staffing pressures through automation to boosting sales with data-driven marketing strategies.
Tips on Strategic Implementation
Maximizing ROI with a Strategic Approach
With a plethora of potentially transformative solutions, restaurant owners should strategically navigate digital transformation:

1. Assess Your Restaurant’s Needs: Evaluate specific challenges and goals before investing in new technology. Understanding your primary pain points, whether inventory management or customer engagement, will help prioritize which technologies to adopt first.

2. Create a Technology Roadmap: Develop a phased plan for technology adoption. Outline which technologies to implement, in what order, and over what timeframe. A gradual, well-planned approach is often more manageable and cost-effective than a complete overhaul.

3. Prioritize Staff Training and Adoption: Advanced technology is only as effective as the people using it. Invest in comprehensive training programs for your staff, ensuring they understand the benefits and correct usage of new tools. Employee buy-in is crucial for successful implementation.

By adhering to these strategies, small- to medium-sized restaurants can more effectively navigate the intricate world of restaurant technology, ensuring substantial returns on their investments through improved operations and enhanced customer experiences.
Future-Proofing Your Independent Restaurant
Balancing Technology and Personalized Service

The relentless march of transformative technology is reshaping every industry, including the restaurant sector. This digital revolution shows no signs of slowing down, potentially propelling the dining experience into an era of unprecedented innovation and efficiency. While keeping your tech stack updated and monitoring emerging trends is essential, the ultimate goal should be to align technology decisions with your restaurant’s unique needs.

During this rush to digitize, it’s crucial not to lose sight of the human touch that defines dining out. The most successful restaurants will strike a balance between technological efficiency and personalized service. Stay agile by regularly reassessing your tech stack and be ready to adapt, but never compromise on the hospitality and personal connections that customers cherish. In the end, technology should enhance, not replace, the human element of your restaurant.

By leveraging the right tools and maintaining a personal touch, you can create a dining environment that is both innovative and authentically yours, a recipe for long-term success in an evolving industry.

title: Predictive Maintenance in Restaurants to Reach USD 107.3B by 2033
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: How AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance is Transforming Restaurant Operations and Reducing Downtime

body.text: How AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance is Transforming Restaurant Operations and Reducing Downtime

Predictive maintenance revolutionizes restaurant operations because the technology prevents equipment failures from occurring. The device is based on artificial intelligence, IoT, and machine learning to analyze the performance of the equipment. It is expected to grow at 28.5% CAGR and reach a value of USD 107.3 billion by 2033. The restaurants have largely adopted this solution to minimize downtime and lower operational costs.
Downtime and Costs

Unplanned equipment failures cause revenue losses and customer losses. Predictive maintenance enables restaurants to monitor kitchen appliances and Point of Sale systems in real time. By identifying potential issues before they lead to failure, businesses can schedule maintenance before they happen. This reduces costly emergency maintenance and extends equipment lifespan, thereby lowering overall operational expenses.
AI and IoT Integration

Predictive maintenance will heavily rely on the uses of artificial intelligence and IoT. Data on appliances in the kitchen, HVAC systems, and refrigerators are sent from smart sensors. Using machine learning algorithms will only come up with patterns and predict possible failure incidents before they happen. This way, restaurant operations become smoothened to increase customer experience and staff productivity.
Key Growth Drivers

There are many reasons why predictive maintenance is on the rise in restaurants. Firstly, it offers efficiency and savings. Increasing labor costs and disruptions in supply chains make preventive measures inevitable. Food safety and equipment maintenance regulations further encourage restaurants to install smart monitoring systems for compliance and efficiency.
Cloud-Based vs. On-Premise Solutions

Predictive maintenance solutions are offered either as cloud-based or on-premise systems. Cloud-based systems provide remote monitoring, automatic updates, and scalability. On-premise systems ensure more control over data security. Restaurants can pick the best alternative based on the operational requirements of the business, budget, and infrastructure capabilities. Cloud-based systems are popularly used due to their flexibility and ease of integration.
Challenges in Implementation

Despite its benefits, predictive maintenance is not without challenges. The first investment in smart sensors and AI-driven software would be costly. Secondly, such restaurants require well-trained personnel to interpret predictive data and allow maintenance work. Data privacy issues and cybersecurity threats require thorough attention to ensure seamless adoption and trust in such technologies.
Impact on Kitchen Equipment

The most essential assets in a kitchen are generally equipment. Predictive maintenance prevents the breakage or breakdown of ovens, fryers, refrigerators, or dishwashers. Systematic monitoring helps ensure that the food preparation continues uninterrupted. Restaurant operators can achieve the goal of maintaining food quality and safety without generating unnecessary waste and operational disruption by reducing unwarranted breakdowns of the equipment.
Improved Customer Experience

Operational efficiency directly impacts customer satisfaction. When equipment functions smoothly, orders are prepared on time, reducing wait times. HVAC and refrigeration systems remain functional, ensuring a comfortable dining environment. Predictive maintenance helps restaurants offer a seamless experience, leading to positive reviews and increased customer loyalty.
Adoption by Large and Small Restaurants

Large restaurant chains are leading the adoption of predictive maintenance due to their ability to invest in advanced technologies. However, small and medium-sized restaurants are also recognizing its value. Cost-effective cloud-based solutions make predictive maintenance accessible to smaller businesses. As technology becomes more affordable, adoption rates are expected to increase across all restaurant segments.
Role in Sustainability Efforts

The restaurant industry is facing the emerging trend of sustainability. Predictive maintenance contributes to being environmentally friendly in the restaurant business by reducing energy and wastage. Energy intake is curbed through efficient machine operation, thereby reducing utility expenses. Emergency repairs are minimized, which reduces the disposal of the equipment, thereby supporting the sustainability objectives. The restaurants can take up this option of predictive maintenance to uphold their environmental responsibility while at the same time increasing profitability.
Near Future Perspective

The future of predictive maintenance in restaurants is promising. Advancements in AI, IoT, and data analytics will enhance predictive accuracy. More restaurants will adopt automation to streamline the process of maintenance. As there is a rise in competition, predictive maintenance will become a standard practice to help restaurants stay ahead. The market's rapid growth reflects the growing importance of technology-driven efficiency in the food service industry.
Conclusion

Predictive maintenance can now revolutionize the restaurant industry, as improvement in efficiency, reduction in costs, and value delivered to customers ensures that restaurants will have fewer equipment failures and operate at a higher level with smoother operations. Increasing AI and IoT means that the future of restaurant management is predisposed to change; therefore, it is inevitable to have good operations.

body.text: Key Drivers and Innovations Shaping the Future of Restaurant Reservation Software

Technological and consumer preference transformations are changing the shape of the restaurant industry. Fundamentally, to this transformational change, modern reservation software systems are being offered, which facilitate the management of business activities by providing better means to improve the customer experience with the ultimate gain of profits. Market estimations have projected the global reservations software market size to be around $95.36 billion in 2024 and reach $258.57 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 13.28% during the period.
Key Growth Drivers for the Market
There are multiple reasons why restaurant reservation software is becoming a hot product to be demanded:

Technological Advancements and Digital Transformation: Cloud computing, mobile applications, artificial intelligence, and data analytics have revolutionized reservation management. Most modern systems offer real-time availability, personalized recommendations, and frictionless integration into other business platforms, which makes them efficient and customer satisfaction enablers.

Change Consumer Behavior and Expectations: Today's consumers expect a convenient and personalized experience, which means they look for easy booking, instant confirmations, and tailored services based on their individual preferences. Reservation software fulfills such expectations through user-friendly interfaces and customized options.

Globalization and Market Growth: Restaurants seeking new markets have increasingly discovered that they need reservation systems that can handle more than one language, currency, and local sensitivities. This feature allows restaurants to service a wide array of customers and ensures a consistent and localized dining experience from one location to another.
Trends in Restaurant Reservation Software
Restaurant reservation software is constantly evolving, and here are a few notable trends:

Mobile Reservations: The growth in smartphone usage has increased mobile bookings. Mobile reservation platforms are designed to be easily accessed on smartphones, making it easier for customers to book tables and thereby increasing access and participation.

Cloud-Based Solutions: With cloud technology, restaurants can be flexible and scalable in terms of managing reservations and tracking guest preferences. It can analyze data in real-time, tremendously reducing the requirement for on-premises hardware, and it becomes easy to update and integrate.

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: AI-based systems can analyze historical booking data, predict demand patterns, optimize table allocations, and personalize customer relationships. AI chatbots, for instance, can answer queries and make reservations while providing personal and efficient experiences when making a booking.

Point of Sale (POS) Systems Integration: The reservation software must be integrated seamlessly with Point of Sale systems, ensuring automatic updates on table availability, menu items, and customer preferences to streamline operations and reduce errors.

Contactless Dining: Health and safety-wise, nearly every reservation platform has come with digital menus, contactless payment options, and even QR code-ordering systems that diminish the need for physical contact and enhance a delicious dining experience.

Data Analytics and Personalization: Advanced analytics enable restaurants to understand customers' behaviors and preferences, creating personalized promotions and loyalty-building operations. This data-driven approach will only strengthen customer relationship building and repeat business.
Challenges Facing the Industry
Even with the benefits, implementing reservation software is not without its challenges:

Integration Complexity: Complex integration of new reservation systems with other existing platforms may be required by property management and customer relationship management tools, which require seamless data exchange to keep them accurate and consistent.

Scalability and Performance: The system must handle peak volumes of bookings without adversely affecting its performance. Architectural issues in the system or network infrastructure could cause slowdowns or even services to become unavailable, thereby affecting customer satisfaction.

Data Security and Compliance: When handling sensitive customer information, data security must be a priority. Therefore, full compliance with regulations like the GDPR and PCI DSS, not to mention regulatory bodies around the world, will be necessary to foster trust and avert legal retribution.
Future Outlook

The restaurant reservation software market has bright prospects, with a rising need for technological advancement and an individualized dining experience. With restaurants competing to meet changing consumer expectations, investment in modern reservation systems is vital. Including these technologies offers operational efficiency and puts businesses in a position to thrive in a competitive and dynamic industry environment.

title: Future-Proofing Restaurants: Key Food Manufacturing Trends to Watch
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Stay Ahead in the Restaurant Industry by Embracing the Latest Food Manufacturing Innovations

body.text: Stay Ahead in the Restaurant Industry by Embracing the Latest Food Manufacturing Innovations

The food manufacturing industry is experiencing rapid change due to automation, AI, and sustainability. To stay on par, restaurants should embrace new technology. Smart kitchen solutions, AI-driven tools, and blockchain will enable efficiency while decreasing restaurant costs and creating trust among customers. Emerging trends must be followed for future-proofing, and restaurant technology must be capitalized upon for ease of operations.
Automation and AI: Optimizing Kitchen Operations

Automation and AI-based tools are transforming the face of food production and restaurant kitchens. AI-driven inventory management tracks stock levels and minimizes waste. Intelligent scheduling software optimizes labor management based on demand patterns. AI-powered analytics enhance menu planning by predicting ingredient usage, ensuring portion control, and reducing costs. Integrating these technologies improves operational efficiency and enhances customer satisfaction.

Automated cooking equipment, such as robotic grills and fryers, ensure consistency but reduce manual labor. AI-based chatbots and innovative ordering systems enhance customer service and speed up service. Restaurant operations that use these solutions will streamline workflows, reduce human error, and enhance productivity. Investing in AI-driven restaurant technology future-proofs operations and improves profit margins.
IoT and Blockchain: Increasing Transparency and Food Safety

IoT and blockchain technologies ensure real-time monitoring for food safety and inventory tracking. IoT-enabled sensors track storage conditions, ensuring that the perishable ingredients remain fresh. Blockchain technology is used for end-to-end traceability, allowing restaurants to verify where their ingredients are coming from and their authenticity. These innovations boost consumer confidence and enhance regulatory compliance.

IoT systems also automate supply chain management, eliminating stock shortages and spoilage. Intelligent alerts inform staff of temperature changes in storage units, cutting down on food waste. Blockchain-based digital records enable restaurants to demonstrate responsible sourcing, strengthening trust with eco-conscious consumers. These technologies are implemented to ensure operational efficiency, food safety, and transparency.
Sustainability: Meeting Eco-Conscious Consumer Expectations

Consumers and restaurants are becoming concerned about sustainability. Manufacturers are accepting schemes for reducing waste, using plant-based ingredients, and offering eco-friendly packages. Restaurateurs must catch up with these trends to source responsibly and adopt sustainable ways. Smart kitchen systems reduce waste and energy and save the environment.

Restaurant food waste tracking AI systems may enable restaurants to automatically identify areas with excess waste and adjust their portion sizes. Restaurants collaborating with food companies using green packaging and environmental-friendly sourcing gain credibility. Consumers opt to spend on businesses that follow sustainability; hence, introducing a restaurant to use green technologies provides efficiency while creating green-conscious consumers for the restaurant to serve.
Clean Labels and Allergen-free Foods- Catering to Dietary Preferences

Consumer demand for clean-label ingredients and allergen-friendly menu options is growing. It now requires restaurants to showcase openness about sourcing ingredients and allergen handling to attract the health-conscious diner. Menu engineering tools use AI to analyze customer preferences, enabling restaurants to adjust to meet demand.

Restaurants offer digital menus that show allergen-free dishes and nutritional information. Customers can scan QR codes that connect to ingredient sourcing details. Training staff on allergen safety and inventory tracking through technology will ensure compliance with dietary requirements. All these efforts create trust and enhance customer satisfaction.
Advanced Food Processing Technologies: Shelf Life Extension

New food processing technologies include High-Pressure Processing (HPP) and Pulsed Electric Fields (PEF), which freshen up ingredients. These methods limit the use of preservatives, thereby increasing shelf life and helping restaurants manage inventory better. Refrigeration systems with IoT sensors monitor storage conditions and ensure that ingredients are of high quality.

Extended shelf-life ingredients reduce spoilage and enable restaurants to plan more flexibly. AI demand forecasting helps restaurants buy ingredients quickly, avoiding overstocking. Advanced food preservation techniques allow restaurants to maintain menu consistency while minimizing waste.
3D Food Printing: Innovating Customization and Efficiency

3D food printing is revolutionizing restaurant kitchens by allowing for the creation of intricate food designs and customized dishes. This technology can enhance presentation, reduce food waste, and ensure portion precision. Restaurants can utilize 3D printing to create unique, Instagram-worthy dishes that attract customers and generate buzz.

Personalized nutrition options allow customers to order food based on their dietary requirements. AI-based customer data analysis helps restaurants identify trends and respond accordingly. Restaurants that include 3D food printing in their operations differentiate themselves and offer innovative dining experiences.
E-commerce and Direct-to-Consumer Trends

Restaurant procurement strategies are being redesigned because direct-to-consumer (DTC) sales are rising in food sales. New innovative supply chain technology empowers restaurants to source fresher ingredients directly from food manufacturers. AI-driven ordering platforms help restaurants streamline procurement by ensuring punctual deliveries and minimizing food waste.

Restaurants can incorporate innovative packaging solutions with freshness indicators for takeout and delivery services. This enhances food quality, improves customer satisfaction, and strengthens brand reputation. By embracing e-commerce innovations, restaurants can stay competitive in an evolving market.
Future Outlook: Embracing Future Food Manufacturing Trends

Restaurant technology is the leader in food manufacturing innovation. Food preparation and service processes are transforming with AI, automation, IoT, and sustainability. All these restaurants will make it efficient, build more trust with their customers, and thus give them a competitive edge over others.

There will always be restaurant technology solutions to invest in the business for advancement continuously. By having data-driven insights, streamlined operations, and innovation, a restaurant would future-proof itself and flourish well in such dynamic markets.

body.text: The Point of Sale market is expanding rapidly, driven by digital payment adoption, cloud-based solutions, and AI-powered transactions.

The global Point of Sale (POS) terminal market is growing rapidly. The adoption of digital payments is driving this growth. Businesses across sectors update their systems to align with customers' changing expectations. The market size is projected to reach $125.30 billion by 2030. During the forecast period, the CAGR is expected to be 8.10%.
Growth Drivers
Growing Digital Payments

The primary market growth drivers are cashless transactions and digital payments. Consumers are using online transactions for contactless convenience, security, and other reasons. Mobile wallets, QR-based payment, and Biometric authentication forms are in increasing demand, further propelling modern Point of Sale terminals with advanced security functionality.
E-commerce and Omni-channel Retail

Online shopping is a trend that has changed the face of business. Organizations are investing in Point of Sale systems that connect online and offline platforms. These systems ensure seamless inventory management and payment processing. Retailers and restaurants use Point of Sale solutions that allow them to offer different modes of payment, including digital wallets and cryptocurrencies.
Cloud-Based Point of Sale Adoption

Cloud-based Point of Sale systems are much more agile and cost-effective than traditional ones. More businesses are accepting this solution mainly because of its flexibility and accessibility from any location. Cloud technology can offer real-time sales monitoring, automatic software updates, and increased data security. Implementing cloud-based Point of Sale platforms has responded to the demand for subscription-based software models.

title: Adapting to Change: How Seattle Restaurants Are Addressing Economic Pressures
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Rising labor costs and economic challenges force restaurants to innovate and redefine the dining experience in 2025

body.text: Rising labor costs and economic challenges force restaurants to innovate and redefine the dining experience in 2025

Soon, people in Seattle will have to get used to a new way of eating out. To deal with rising labor costs and other economic problems, restaurants are reviewing their business plans again. Local businesses already use new ideas to stay profitable and meet customers' changing needs.

This is what Anthony Anton, president and CEO of the Washington Hospitality Association, said not long ago. He bravely said that most tests on restaurant models would be done by 2025, which meant that things had to change.
"There will be plenty of failed innovations about new ideas and models," he said. "The employees will approve some, and some workers and consumers won't stand it."
Impact of Rising Minimum Wage and Tip Credit Loss

Restaurants are already struggling because wages are going up. From now on, workers must be paid at least $20.76 an hour. Last year, businesses were only required to pay $17.25 an hour, and tips could be used to pay workers' wages.
This means businesses must pay each worker an extra $3.51 an hour. Because of inflation and rising food prices, small companies must change how they do business.
New Restaurant Models Gaining Momentum
Even though Seattle restaurants are feeling the economy's effects, new types of places are opening up. Some of these are self-order kiosks, digital menus, and hybrid dining forms.
Customers can order at the bar and have full-service dinners at hybrid models. The restaurants will have places to eat inside and a store where food can be bought to go.
"People are taking great leaps to come up with something that customers and employees can accept," he remarked. "The bottom line is to find a model which sustains their business dreams."
Restaurants with regular buildings will soon partner with food trucks that serve the same kind of food. Ghost Kitchens is another newcomer. It has self-order booths and places for customers to wait.
Balancing Innovation with Survival
Anton points out that not every trial will work. If nothing changes, the number of places in town will go down.
Anton told us that restaurant sales might decrease by 4 to 9 percent. The other businesses would also be more open because buyers would spread around them.
Anton seems optimistic about the uncertainty. Thanks to new ideas, the will-to-change business will be able to join the wagon, he thinks.
Educational Initiatives for Restaurant Owners

The Washington Hospitality Association is starting a series of educational videos to help restaurant owners cope with these changes. The series will show effective methods and suggest new business strategies.
"We're putting together videos to show what different operators are trying," said the man. "We're also looking for more people to volunteer their ideas and concepts."
By providing them with this information, they aim to encourage more restaurant owners to try models that might work for them.
A Plea For Patience
Anton asks people in Seattle to be patient as the food scene changes. He thinks these changes will not always work out well but are necessary for the business to stay alive.
"There's a great deal of opportunity and uncertainty ahead," he remarked. "We ask for a bit of grace as restaurants experiment and find what works."

Seattle's dining experience is changing, but the local operators show no signs of slowing down; they are innovative and adaptable, embracing new models and learning from each other as they strive for a sustainable future for the restaurant industry.

Growing Demand for Self-Service Solutions

Self-service technology has been accelerating over the past few years. Companies are adopting kiosks to enhance customer engagement, decrease waiting time, and simplify processes. These systems allow users to perform tasks such as ordering food, making payments, or checking in for appointments more quickly and efficiently.

Customers are increasingly seeking touchless and hassle-free services. Hence, the kiosk market has grown quite well. Therefore, the trend will continue, with the kiosk market growing consistently over time.

Innovation plays a critical role in expanding the kiosk market. Sophisticated technology makes kiosks flexible, efficient, and user-friendly. Industry-wise, the features that are now gradually becoming norms of the industry include touchscreen interfaces, integrated payment systems, and AI-driven personalization.

For example, AI-enabled kiosks are capable of analyzing consumer behavior and preferences and making recommendations. Touchless technology was in the limelight during the pandemic; it is now trending. It is these trends and features that infuse the same appeal for businesses and consumers to brands. Projected to grow at 6.1% CAGR

Automation happens to be one of the major drivers of this expansion as businesses are keen to streamline their operations and bring down dependency on human labor.

The cost-effectiveness of kiosks has also increased, and thus the reach has been made easier for small and medium-sized businesses. All these, combined with increasing consumer demand for self-service options, are pushing the market forward.
Industries Adopting Kiosk Solutions
Kiosks are being used in various industries, and each is finding its unique applications for the technology.

Retail: Kiosks are used by retailers as sales channels for easy checkout and personalization in shopping. Interactive kiosks allow searching inventory, ordering, and even offering a customization option.

Healthcare: Hospitals and clinics use kiosks to enable patient check-in, bill payments, and scheduling of appointments. These devices help reduce administrative burdens and enhance service efficiency.

Foodservice: Restaurants, particularly quick-service chains, implement kiosks to facilitate quicker ordering and payment. The systems cut down wait times and ensure higher accuracy of orders, leading to enhanced customer satisfaction.

As more applications for kiosks open up, businesses will discover new ways to adapt kiosks to their business.

New opportunities are arising, particularly in the area of demand for sustainable and energy-efficient kiosks. Manufacturers are exploring eco-friendly materials and energy-saving technologies for such demands. These innovations not only reduce operational costs but will also attract environmentally conscious customers.
Future of Kiosk Market

Diversify Your Supplier Relationships

While it might be well for most of the year, the holiday season's peak demand might expose you to issues that you might not anticipate. To avoid running out of critical inventory, you must diversify your supplier relationships.

Maintaining a list of trusted backup vendors ensures you have alternatives in place. Even if you like working with specific suppliers, having contingency options can protect your restaurant from last-minute disruptions.
Invest in Smart Inventory Management

The holiday season demands a good stock level, so avoiding stockouts requires smart inventory management. The rising demand during this period requires using smart inventory management tools that can keep you ahead of the game. A modern restaurant management system provides features such as:

items: Tracking and viewing real-time inventory as their levels change.
Demand can be forecasted from historic trends through the use of predictive analytics.
Automated reorders help in maintaining a balanced stock level.

body.text: Making use of such tools would make the person operating the restaurant exceptionally well, zeroing in on waste levels and guaranteeing that his business will be maximized by fully operating it over the holiday.
Applying Advanced Forecasting Techniques
Predictive planning will help fight against supply chain interruption. Advanced techniques in forecasting create future demand through historical levels and existing patterns in the market.

With the help of forecasting tools, you can adjust your purchasing decisions, predict ingredient shortages, and prepare for seasonal demand fluctuations. You can also analyze past data to identify which menu items are likely to experience a surge in orders and thus plan for them.
Be Flexible with Technology

Technology has played a big role in supporting restaurants in achieving supply chain stability. Cloud-based solutions enable inventory remote monitoring, tracking of orders, and real-time communication with the suppliers.

The order streaming, tracking deliveries, and responsive nature to any interruption when using digital channels of communication with the suppliers. With such flexibility brought about by technology, there is a timely reaction to avoid service interruptions or ensure that customer expectations are met.
Seasonal Menu Adaptation

One flexible menu can help lessen supply chain stress over the holiday. You can create one menu that can easily replace the ingredients to change what you're offering when certain ingredients come off backorder.

Seasonal ingredients can also make inventory relatively easy to manage while fitting the preferences of consumers. Use past data to identify the least likely ingredients to be available during a certain period and order replacement ingredients ahead of time.
In addition, maintain open communication with suppliers.

In the supply chain challenges, always have good supplier relationships. This is because it ensures there is open communication where, if there is an issue that may arise, both parties are aware of it, thus working together to resolve the challenge.

Schedule regular check-ins with your suppliers and work together on contingency plans. Technology solutions that integrate supplier communication can also provide real-time updates, keeping you well-informed and prepared for any disruptions.
Train Your Staff for Better Preparedness

While technology and supplier strategies are critical, your employees need to be ready to handle the increase in demand. Proper training would ensure that all your employees become conversant with inventory management procedures and make the best use of restaurant technology.

Empower the staff to monitor the inventory and identify bottlenecks in the supply chain so that you do not face bottlenecks and ensure smooth operations. The employees will be able to make quick decisions to keep the restaurant running smoothly during peak hours.
Prepare for a Successful Holiday Season

Do not worry when holidays are coming around. Using wise and intelligent inventory control strategies, with friendly supplier relationships and in cooperation with some excellent tools developed to allow proper forecasting, you are certainly bound to bank on better control of surging orders during such times.
Proper preparation holds the key to letting your restaurant excel this holiday season as well as assure quality service to clients.

To meet demand during this time, strategic planning is key, and the data from your Point of Sale (POS) system can be your best ally. Analyze Past Holiday Sales Trends

Historical sales data is also a motherlode of forecasting information. Analysis of past holiday seasons helps identify peak times to dine, menu preferences, and revenue patterns. Indeed, sales trends by day of the week or time of day can pinpoint busy weekends just before Christmas, for example. This kind of information allows restaurants to prepare for traffic patterns, setting them up to meet customer expectations.
Seasonalize Your Menu

Holiday diners tend to flock toward seasonal favorites, so it is the perfect time to update your menu. Analyze which dishes, drinks, or desserts were the most popular in previous years. Be it a signature entrée, a festive cocktail, or a unique dessert offering, aligning your menu with past preferences will ensure you capture customers' attention and satisfy their cravings.
This data-driven strategy also fosters creativity. Try introducing novel items that mirror current trends but are also consistent with what was popular last season.
Optimize Staffing

Holiday parties, from office parties to family suppers, usually have larger guest counts. Point of Sale reporting can predict peak reservation times, allowing managers to make staffing decisions accordingly. Restaurants can deliver exceptional service during these busy seasons without forcing their staff too hard by planning ahead.

Balanced scheduling is beneficial for the restaurant and for the employees. A prepared staff can provide high-quality service, thereby pleasing customers and saving employees from burnout in the week when business is extremely high.
Effectively Manage Inventories

Running out of key ingredients during the holiday season is a restaurateur's worst nightmare. Using historical sales data, you can estimate the inventory needs for festive favorites and ensure sufficient stock. At the same time, precise forecasting prevents overordering, reducing waste and storage challenges.

For instance, if past analysis indicates raised demand for certain seasonal goods such as cranberries, turkey, or special type desserts. You can put orders in advance and ensure that the services run smoothly during the season.

While historical data is very important, real-time monitoring is also crucial. Holidays are very unpredictable. Weather changes may occur, and there may arise last-minute reservations. In some instances, customer preferences may change during the last minute.

The Point of Sale system allows managers to see sales in action, thus allowing for immediate reaction. For example, if one menu item is running significantly higher than projected, they can adjust their orders for inventory or the quantities that need to be prepared.

body.text: Proactive Food Safety Practices to Safeguard Your Restaurant

In 2024, food safety has undergone significant changes due to technological innovations. However, foodborne illnesses are still a pressing concern for the restaurant industry. Although there are automated monitoring sensors and light-based decontamination systems, a preventive approach is still the heart of food safety. Here is how restaurant managers can protect their business and their customers.
Foodborne Illness Basics

Foodborne illnesses, also known as food poisoning, are caused by the consumption of contaminated food or drinks. They are caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites and affect approximately 48 million people in the United States annually, according to the CDC. In addition to health concerns, these illnesses cost the economy an estimated $15 billion annually, making vigilance a critical need.

It would be of great importance to have restaurant managers understand the causes, symptoms, and consequences associated with foodborne illnesses. A single instance can hurt not only your patrons but also your restaurant's reputation and bottom line.
Key Strategies for Prevention
1\. Source Ingredients Wisely

Food safety starts with sourcing. Select suppliers that have recognized certifications such as GFSI or SQF audit the practices of their suppliers regularly and require documentation to establish compliance.
The Food Traceability Rule of the FSMA enhances traceability records starting January 2026. Following these standards will keep you a step ahead of the changing regulations.
2\. Store Food Correctly
Correct storage will prevent bacterial growth. Store cold foods at or below 40°F and hot foods at 140°F or higher.
Here's how to store certain foods safely:
Meat and Poultry: Keep in covered containers on the bottom shelves so that they don't come into contact with other foods.
Dairy Products: Place in the coldest portion of the refrigerator. Don't store in the door.
Produce: Wash it well and store it away from raw meats.
3\. Create a Food Safety Culture

A safety-first attitude should be embedded in the kitchen. There should be open communication on safety concerns, and employees should not fear to voice their opinion on issues. Hold regular refreshers on food safety to ensure the issue remains at the top of their minds.
Food safety culture promotes accountability and awareness, thereby reducing the risks. In the kitchen, there should be ownership of food safety practices.
What to Do If There Is an Outbreak
Although prevention is the best medicine, no restaurant can prepare for worst-case scenarios. An incident management plan is critical to effective foodborne illness complaints management.
Steps to Manage a Potentially Outbreak Situation:
Record Complaints in Detail: Record the customer's contact details, meal details, and symptoms.
Contact Health Authorities: Notifying local health departments will seek guidance and assistance.
Keep it Transparent: Prepare a public statement that outlines the nature of the problem and how it is being dealt with.
Remaining calm and taking proactive steps in such circumstances helps to reduce damage to your restaurant's reputation and reassures customers of your commitment to safety.
Food Safety through Technology

Food safety can be enhanced through the use of technology. Automated temperature monitoring systems and food labeling solutions can make compliance easy. Light-based decontamination systems add another layer of protection for food contact surfaces.
By implementing these tools in proactive ways, restaurants can have added layers of security against foodborne illness without getting inefficient.
Takeaway

Foodborne illnesses represent one of the major challenges, and having proactive measures protects your restaurant. Sourcing the best ingredient, instilling a culture of safety, and preparing for emergencies-all these measures safeguard your customers as well as your brand.

Investing in food safety is less about complying than it's about winning hearts and setting up the basis for ultimate success. So make food safety a priority, and inform your customers that well-being's always on the menu.

body.text: Efficiency at What Cost? The Hidden Downsides of Self-Service Kiosks in Restaurants

In recent years, the fast-paced adoption of self-service kiosks in the restaurant industry has been praised for its potential to streamline operations and address staffing shortages. However, a recent study conducted by experts in food and beverage marketing has unveiled an unexpected drawback: the social dynamics of lines at automated kiosks can lead to a decrease in customer spending. This article explores the surprising downside of self-service kiosks and suggests ways that restaurants can mitigate these issues.
The Pressure of the Line

When customers use self-service kiosks to place their orders, a common occurrence is the formation of lines behind them. According to the study, the presence of people waiting imposes an unspoken pressure on the customer using the kiosk to hurry through their decision-making process.
"We found that when customers perceive that they are holding up the line, they feel rushed and tend to make quicker, less considered decisions," says one of the study’s authors.

This phenomenon leads customers to opt for familiar items they know well, rather than taking the time to browse through the menu and consider new or additional items. As a result, spending decreases because customers are not exploring the full range of options available to them.
A Psychological Battle

To delve deeper into this issue, researchers conducted three experiments involving hundreds of participants who were asked to imagine themselves in various restaurant scenarios. Overwhelmingly, participants reported feeling pressured to order quickly when there was a visible queue behind them. This implicates a significant psychological component: the fear of social judgment from those waiting.

"As people generally aim to be considerate of others, they inadvertently end up rushing their own experience, possibly missing out on items they might have enjoyed, ergo contributing to lower overall sales for the restaurant," explained the study.
The Single Line Solution

One proposed solution to alleviate this pressure is the implementation of a single queue that serves multiple kiosks. This arrangement distributes the wait time among all customers, rather than placing the full burden on the individual currently placing their order.

With multiple kiosks fed by a single line, customers don’t feel as targeted or stressed about holding up others. This not only reduces the emotional rush experienced by the person at the kiosk but also boosts their confidence to explore the menu more thoroughly.
Systemic Communication

Another effective fix involves kiosk interface design. Researchers suggest that a simple pop-up message could significantly mitigate perceived pressure. This message would communicate that the restaurant takes full responsibility for any delays during the ordering process, reassuring customers that they are not at fault for the longer wait times.

When customers feel that the blame for any hold-up doesn't lie on their shoulders, they can take their time, potentially increasing both customer satisfaction and sales. The psychological effect of feeling supported by the business can create a more relaxed and enjoyable ordering experience.
Broader Implications

The study’s findings highlight an important aspect of the evolving intersection between technology and consumer behavior. For restaurant owners considering the transition to automated systems, it's critical to understand these social dynamics to avoid unintended consequences.

"As we seek to make the dining experience more efficient through self-service technology, we must not overlook the human factors at play," advises the research team. "Design choices that address these social dynamics can lead to a more effective and customer-friendly self-service system."
Conclusion

While self-service kiosks offer numerous advantages, such as improved operational efficiency and a solution to staffing issues, restaurants must be mindful of the hidden challenges these systems can introduce. By adopting strategies like single lines to serve multiple kiosks and using supportive messaging within the interface, restaurants can enhance the customer experience, leading to increased satisfaction and spending.

Incorporating these elements into the design and layout of self-service systems addresses both operational and psychological aspects, ensuring that the benefits of automation do not come at the cost of customer engagement and revenue.

author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Introduction to Avocado Oil: Understanding Its Purity

body.text: Introduction to Avocado Oil: Understanding Its Purity

Avocado oil has surged in popularity in recent years, praised for its heart-healthy properties and mild flavor. However, recent scientific analysis reveals that much of the avocado oil available in stores is adulterated, misleading consumers who believe they are purchasing pure avocado oil.
Rampant Adulteration in Avocado Oil
UC-Davis Study Reveals Grim Findings

Scientists at the University of California at Davis conducted comprehensive tests on avocado oil samples and identified alarming levels of adulteration and mislabeling. The study revealed that 21 out of 36 bottles tested, approximately two-thirds, were found to be adulterated with cheaper seed and vegetable oils, and sometimes oils that could pose risks to individuals with food sensitivities.
Retailers Involved in Selling Adulterated Products

The study pointed fingers at some of the largest retail chains in the U.S. and Canada, including Walmart, Sam’s Club, Kroger, and Safeway. These retailers did not respond to requests for comments, while others dispute the findings or cite supply chain complexities.
How Cheap Avocado Oil is Made
Unrefined vs. Refined Avocado Oil
The quality of avocado oil varies widely depending on the type of processing:

items: Unrefined Oils: These are typically labeled as virgin or extra virgin. They are minimally processed, preserving more nutrients and a green tint.
Refined Oils: Highly processed using methods like bleaching and deodorizing, these oils are less nutrient-dense and neutral in flavor.

body.text: The Risks of Misleading Labels

Adulterated oils not only deceive consumers but also pose health risks, particularly for those with food sensitivities. More concerning is the use of cheaper oils like sunflower, safflower, and canola by unscrupulous suppliers looking to profit.
Suppliers Selling Fake Avocado Oil

According to industry experts, the pervasive adulteration isn't a secret. Ben Barnard, founder and chairman of AvoPacific, a leading avocado oil producer, noted that prices offered by some competitors are suspiciously low, indicating potential adulteration to cut costs.
The Adulterated Avocado Oil Brands

In response to calls for transparency, UC-Davis disclosed the brands that failed their tests. Retailers implicated include Walmart, Trader Joe’s, Aldi, Metro, Meijer, and Kroger. The most frequent adulterants identified were sunflower, safflower, canola, and soybean oils.
Examples of Adulterated Products
Among the worst offenders was Stop & Shop’s store-brand “extra-virgin” avocado oil, which despite its high price, was found to contain oils that were not even avocado oil.
Retailers’ Reactions to Study Findings

Most retailers, such as Trader Joe’s and Metro, insist their products meet quality standards based on certifications from suppliers and third-party labs. However, these guarantees are often based on outdated or incomplete testing and do not account for the findings from the recent UC-Davis study.
Statements from Retailers
Retailers provided mixed responses:

items: Stop & Shop: Claimed they no longer used the implicated supplier and have switched to routine testing.
Trader Joe’s: Stated reliance on industry-standard testing but did not retest old batches.
Metro: Asserted compliance based on tests from their own records and recent government inspections.

body.text: The Need for Better Oversight and Independent Testing

Selina Wang, the UC-Davis scientist leading the research, emphasized that retailers should not rely solely on supplier certifications, advocating for routine independent testing to validate product integrity. This measure would be a significant step toward ensuring consumers get what they believe they are buying.

The rampant adulteration of avocado oil is an issue that needs industry-wide attention and stricter regulatory oversight. Consumers deserve transparency and accuracy in food labeling, and it’s imperative that both retailers and suppliers work together to ensure the products on store shelves meet the quality promised on their labels.

One effective solution is to have a single line of waiting customers lead to multiple kiosks, rather than each kiosk having its own dedicated line. This approach ensures that customers feel less responsible for holding up the line, thereby providing them with a more relaxed ordering experience.
Experts in Food and Beverage Marketing Weigh In

As experts in food and beverage marketing with a focus on self-service technology, we have observed a rising trend among restaurants to implement automated processes. This trend aims to streamline ordering and address staffing shortages, ultimately placing more control in the hands of customers. However, an unintended consequence of this shift is the added pressure customers feel to expedite their orders, resulting in less thoughtful choices and lower spending.
Three Experiments Highlight Customer Behavior

To delve deeper into this issue, we conducted three experiments involving hundreds of participants. These experiments required participants to imagine waiting in line at a restaurant in different scenarios. The results confirmed that the presence of a queue led most people to feel pressured to order quickly. This pressure resulted in hastier decisions and reduced overall spending.
Mitigating the Pressure: Two Effective Solutions

The experiments revealed two potential strategies for mitigating this pressure. Firstly, creating a single line that serves multiple kiosks can distribute the waiting time more evenly and reduce individual stress. Secondly, displaying a pop-up message on the kiosk interface, assuring customers that the business takes full responsibility for any service delays, can also alleviate the perceived need to rush.
Implications for Effective Self-Service Design

Our research highlights the social dynamics at play in self-service ordering systems and offers valuable insights for designing a more effective and customer-friendly process. It alerts restaurant owners to the potential unintended consequences associated with the transition to automated technology and underscores the importance of thoughtful system redesigns to enhance customer experience and satisfaction.

The findings of this study suggest that while self-service kiosks can address certain operational challenges, they must be implemented in a way that considers the psychological and social dynamics of the customer experience. By doing so, restaurants can better navigate the complexities of automated ordering systems and ultimately drive more thoughtful purchases and higher customer satisfaction.

title: Combining Delivery Orders Results in Extended Times, Poorer Quality
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: When Faster Isn’t Better: The Hidden Costs of Bundled Deliveries

body.text: When Faster Isn’t Better: The Hidden Costs of Bundled Deliveries

Secret shoppers in a study from Intouch Insight were far less satisfied when their meal arrived after others were dropped off along the way, a common practice for apps like DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub. This story is part of a series based on The Path to Third-Party Excellence, an upcoming secret shopper study from Intouch Insight conducted exclusively for Restaurant Business and its sister publications CSP Daily News and Nation's Restaurant News.
Impact on Delivery Times and Food Quality

Third-party delivery providers’ practice of bundling multiple orders in one trip slows delivery times and hurts customer satisfaction, according to the Intouch Insight report. The study, which used secret shoppers to place 600 delivery orders from restaurants and convenience stores across the U.S., illustrates the drawbacks of order batching, a tactic that has long been used by restaurant delivery apps but is rarely discussed openly.
The Scope of the Study

The Intouch Insight shoppers were instructed to order from whatever establishment they wished, but they couldn’t use a paid membership or pay extra for a direct delivery. The results showed that 12% of orders were picked up and delivered by a courier who first made other drop-offs along the way. Shoppers were notified within the app when this was the case.
Longer Last Leg and Compromised Quality

Per the results, the last leg of a batched delivery took more than 42 minutes to complete, on average, or more than 13 minutes longer than orders that traveled directly to the customer. This delay negatively impacted the food, with the temperature correct only 77% of the time for batched deliveries compared to 95% for direct deliveries. Customer satisfaction also took a hit, with overall satisfaction at 79% for batched orders, 10 points lower than for nonstop orders.
Frequency of Batching by App

According to the Intouch Insight results, batching was fairly common, though the frequency differed by app: 19% of orders placed with Uber Eats were part of a batched delivery compared to 12% for DoorDash and 5% for Grubhub.
Responses from Delivery Apps

A DoorDash representative said several factors dictate when orders are batched but did not elaborate. Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi previously mentioned that the company uses artificial intelligence to determine when to bundle orders. Both representatives emphasized that batching is designed to get customers their orders faster during busy periods.
A Grubhub spokesperson said 86% of the company’s overall orders arrive on time but did not provide a figure for batched orders.
The Challenges for Restaurants

“\[Batched delivery\] is not working for the customer,” said Sarah Beckett, director of marketing at Intouch Insight. “But also, the other element of it for the restaurant or the convenience store is, how do they protect their reputation, their brand, when some of this stuff is really taken out of their control?”
One suggested solution is to invest in better packaging to ensure food stays fresh during trips with multiple stops.
The Bigger Picture

These findings highlight another potential pain point in the relationship between restaurants and third-party delivery providers. Though the apps have become an important revenue channel for many operators since the pandemic, some complain about high delivery commissions, lack of data on their delivery customers, and a loss of control once an order leaves their store.

Yet, the results also show that consumers are generally quite happy with the third-party delivery experience. Shoppers’ overall satisfaction with restaurant delivery across all three apps was 91%, a 4-point improvement from 2022, when Intouch Insight last measured it.
Conclusion

As third-party delivery continues to grow, the industry must address the negative impacts of batching on both delivery times and food quality. Restaurants may need to find innovative ways to ensure their food arrives fresh, while the delivery apps must balance cost efficiency with customer happiness to maintain their share of this increasingly competitive market.

author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Choosing Secure IoT Devices for Your Restaurant

body.text: Choosing Secure IoT Devices for Your Restaurant

The restaurant industry, known for its razor-thin margins and relentless pace, is increasingly turning to technology to optimize operations and enhance the customer experiences. The Internet of Things (IoT), with its promise of interconnected devices and data-driven insights, is rapidly transforming how restaurants operate, from the kitchen to the dining room and beyond. However, this digital transformation introduces new and evolving cybersecurity risks that demand a nuanced and proactive security strategy.
The Expanding Attack Surface

While connected thermostats and security systems, point-of-sale (POS) systems, and customer Wi-Fi hotspots offer undeniable benefits - remote monitoring, real-time data analysis, and enhanced customer engagement - they also expand the attack surface, creating new entry points for cybercriminals. Add to the mix the rapid adoption of such IoT devices as ordering kiosks, inventory management sensors, and robotic servers and chefs, and that attack surface increases by orders of magnitude. Traditional cybersecurity measures, primarily designed to protect static IT infrastructures, often prove inadequate in addressing the unique vulnerabilities of these interconnected devices.
Complexity and Resource Constraints

Consider the typical restaurant IT environment: a complex network of stationary computers, mobile tablets used by waitstaff, connected kitchen appliances, and guest-facing Wi-Fi hotspots. Each device, with its own operating system, software vulnerabilities, and communication protocols, presents a potential point of compromise. Adding to the complexity, many restaurants lack dedicated IT personnel, relying instead on staff with limited cybersecurity expertise to manage these systems.
A Tailored Approach to IoT Security

This is where a tailored approach to IoT security becomes paramount. Rather than relying on generic security solutions, restaurants need to adopt a multi-layered strategy that addresses the specific challenges posed by these interconnected devices.
Visibility: The Foundation of Effective IoT Security

The first step towards securing any network, especially one as dynamic as a restaurant’s, is establishing complete visibility. This means knowing exactly what devices are connected to the network, what software they are running, and how they are communicating with each other. Network discovery tools, capable of automatically identifying and profiling devices, are essential in this regard. These tools provide a real-time inventory of all connected assets, including those often overlooked, such as smart appliances and security cameras.
Moving Beyond Basic Threat Detection

Once visibility is established, the next step is implementing robust threat detection mechanisms. Traditional signature-based antivirus software, while still relevant, is often insufficient in detecting the sophisticated attacks targeting IoT devices. This is where machine learning and artificial intelligence come into play. By analyzing network traffic patterns and device behavior, these technologies can identify anomalies that might indicate malicious activity, even if the attack signature is unknown.
The Importance of Automated Response

Detecting a threat is only half the battle. Equally crucial is the ability to respond swiftly and effectively. In the fast-paced environment of a restaurant, every second counts. Automated response mechanisms, triggered by pre-defined rules or machine learning algorithms, can isolate compromised devices, block malicious traffic, and even shut down critical systems to prevent further damage. This proactive approach, rather than a reactive one, is essential in minimizing the impact of a cyberattack.
Empowering Existing IT Teams

While a dedicated IoT security team might seem ideal, it’s not always feasible for restaurants operating with limited resources. This is where user-friendly, centralized security platforms prove invaluable. title: New Study Reveals AI Label May Deter Consumers
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Impact of AI Labeling on Purchasing Decisions

body.text: Impact of AI Labeling on Purchasing Decisions
Even as tech giants pour billions of dollars into what they herald as humanity’s new frontier, a recent study shows that tacking the “AI” label on products may actually drive people away.
Findings of the Study

A study published in the Journal of Hospitality Marketing & Management in June found that describing a product as using AI lowers a customer’s intention to buy it. Researchers sampled participants across various age groups and showcased the same products - the only difference being one described as “high tech” and the other as using AI, or artificial intelligence.

“We looked at vacuum cleaners, TVs, consumer services, health services,” said Dogan Gursoy, one of the study’s authors. “In every single case, the intention to buy or use the product or service was significantly lower whenever we mentioned AI in the product description.”

Despite AI’s rapid advancement in recent months, the study highlights consumers’ hesitance to incorporate AI into their daily lives, a marked divergence from the enthusiasm driving innovations in big tech.
The Role of Trust

The study delved into how participants viewed products considered “low risk,” like household appliances using AI, and “high risk,” such as self-driving cars, AI-powered investment decision-making services, and medical diagnosis services. Non-buyers were the majority in both product groups, with a higher rejection rate in the high-risk category.
There are two kinds of trust that the study identifies as influencing consumers' perception of AI-powered products:

1. Cognitive Trust: This type of trust is associated with the expectation that AI, as a machine, should be free from human error. When AI makes mistakes, the eroded trust can be significant. For example, AI-generated search results that provide incorrect information can quickly diminish trust in the technology.

2. Emotional Trust: Limited knowledge and understanding about AI compel consumers to rely on emotional trust, making subjective judgments about the technology. Fear of the unknown plays a crucial role here. Gursoy points out that even before public awareness of tools like AI chatbots, AI had been running in the background for years without much public knowledge.
Pop culture, particularly Hollywood science fiction films portraying robots as villains, has significantly influenced public perception of AI, adding to the general mistrust.
Lack of Transparency

Another major factor influencing customers is the perceived risk around AI, especially concerning data privacy. Consumer concerns about how companies handle their personal data have dampened enthusiasm for AI tools that aim to streamline user experience. This lack of transparency could sour customers' perceptions toward even well-established brands.

Gursoy emphasizes the importance of transparency, advising companies against using “AI” as a mere buzzword without elaborating on its capabilities. “The most advisable thing for them to do is come up with the right messaging,” he said. “Rather than simply putting ’AI-powered’ or ’run by AI,’ telling people how this can help them will ease the consumer’s fears.”
Conclusion

While AI technology continues to advance rapidly, bridging the gap between innovation and consumer trust remains crucial. Companies aiming to incorporate AI into their products must carefully consider how they communicate these advances to avoid alienating potential buyers.

title: Farewell to Al Fresco: NYC Begins Phasing Out Outdoor Dining Sheds
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: From Streets to Sidewalks: Adapting to New Norms

body.text: From Streets to Sidewalks: Adapting to New Norms

The majority of New York City restaurants participating in the city’s pandemic-era outdoor dining program did not seek permits to make their sheds permanent, requiring these structures to be dismantled. By the August 3 deadline, only about 2,600 dining establishments applied for the permits, according to the city Department of Transportation (DOT). This number is less than half of the estimated 6,000 to 8,000 restaurants currently using outdoor dining permits issued since 2020.
Heated Debates and New Regulations

The deadline concludes months of intense debate among stakeholders on maintaining the vibrant outdoor dining culture that thrived during the pandemic. Critics argue the structures are unsightly, attract rodents, and occupy valuable parking spaces. Conversely, supporters believe they enliven the cityscape and provide crucial support to small businesses.

Under the new Dining Out NYC program, roadway sheds must be disassembled and stored from late November through March. Restaurants must also meet new specifications for their structures, such as ensuring they are not fully enclosed, requiring some to rebuild their sheds.
Financial and Logistical Challenges for Restaurants

Just over 1,300 permit applications are for roadway sheds, and about 2,000 are for sidewalk seating, which has more lenient, year-round rules. Manny Colon, owner of Manny’s Bistro on the Upper West Side, applied for both roadway and sidewalk permits, which cost $1,050 each for four years, a reduced fee compared to pre-Covid prices.

The new regulations pose significant financial and logistical challenges. Colon estimates a city-approved contractor would charge $40,000 to dismantle, rebuild, and store his shed for the winter. Instead, he opted for a more cost-effective solution, asking a friend to modify plywood and using a U-Haul to transport the shed to his daughter's house upstate for storage. Despite cutting costs, he will still spend $25,000 and will have to reduce his roadway seating due to new size restrictions.
Industry Reactions and Calls for Program Tweaks

Although Colon expects to turn a profit, he acknowledges the complications. "It’s quite complicated, and that’s why a lot of restaurants are just going to focus on the sidewalk," he remarked. Colon is pleased the city is enforcing rules to improve safety, especially concerning hazardous structures encroaching into bike lanes.

Andrew Rigie, executive director of the New York City Hospitality Alliance, highlighted the low application rates as a sign that the program needs adjustments. “There are many parts of the new outdoor dining law that are much better than the pre-pandemic sidewalk café law, but despite the DOT’s outreach and collaboration, too few eligible small businesses have applied,” Rigie noted. He emphasized the need for the city to analyze the low participation and adjust the rules to achieve a more inclusive outdoor dining initiative.
Official Response and Future Plans

City officials maintain that the number of applications is still double the participation rates from before the pandemic. "The new program preserves what New Yorkers came to love about outdoor dining while addressing important quality-of-life issues," said a transportation department spokesperson.
As New York City transitions away from its pandemic-era outdoor dining program, the ongoing discussions and adaptations will shape the future landscape of dining in the city.

These platforms enable centralized management of branding assets, ensuring that all locations apply the same visuals and messaging, with so many restaurant brands having locations in different regions of the country, this is an especially helpful feature. Additionally, utilizing technology allows businesses more insight on customer trends and behaviors, which gives a leg up on competitors who aren’t receiving any feedback or analytics on their marketing and branding efforts.

Ultimately, leveraging technology not only benefits operational efficiency but also strengthens brand perception and customer engagement across all locations, which gives a brand a competitive edge in a crowded market.

Effective brand management requires consistent and cohesive visual and digital assets across all touchpoints, from in-store signage to online/social media marketing campaigns. When a business uses a technology-driven brand management platform, it gains access to a centralized hub for branded and customizable marketing assets.

These systems provide a secure location for logos, taglines, promotional materials, color schemes, and more, that are accessible to authorized users across the system. This means that individual locations can customize assets while adhering to set brand guidelines, thus enhancing brand visibility regardless of geographical location.

The strongest brands strike a balance between consistency and personalization. By leveraging a technology-driven centralized hub, businesses can maintain consistency while simultaneously adapting marketing strategies to meet evolving consumer preferences and market trends. This provides a significant advantage over competitors who either ignore the wants and needs of consumers in different markets or neglect brand guidelines altogether resulting in marketing inconsistency.

By adopting brand management platforms as a resource, multi-location businesses can streamline the creation and implementation of marketing materials, maintain the control of assets, and enforce brand guidelines consistently across locations. Technology is a game changer when it comes to businesses having access to real-time analytics. Additionally, optimizing the use of nearby resources means that businesses can minimize their carbon footprint, aligning with broader sustainability goals.

Overall, brand management platforms are pivotal in enhancing operational efficiency for multi-location businesses, offering a seamless solution for producing and distributing essential marketing materials while also promoting sustainability through localized production and streamlined supply chain operations.

title: Digital Temptations: How Online Food Ordering Boosts Indulgence and Spending Habits
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Unveiling the Research on Digital Food Ordering Habits

body.text: Unveiling the Research on Digital Food Ordering Habits

As restaurants increasingly embrace technology for placing food orders, a new University of South Florida study reveals that digital ordering platforms significantly influence consumer behavior, often leading to more indulgent food choices and increased spending.
Study Overview and Key Findings

Co-authored by Dipayan Biswas, the USF Frank Harvey endowed professor of marketing in the Muma College of Business, the comprehensive study compares the cognitive effects of ordering from a digital screen to traditional methods, including printed menus.

The research, published in the Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, highlights the shift towards digital ordering in major food chains introducing touchscreen kiosks and tabletop tablets. The growth of app-based delivery services such as Uber Eats, Grubhub, and DoorDash since the COVID-19 pandemic further illustrates this trend.
Pandemic-Induced Changes in Food Acquisition

According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture Economic Research Service, the pandemic significantly altered how U.S. consumers acquire food, particularly through carryout and delivery services. Spending on third-party delivery tripled for quick-service restaurants and nearly quadrupled for full-service restaurants from pre-pandemic levels to late 2022.

"While digital ordering can enhance convenience and efficiency, many consumers will opt for unhealthier food choices and spend more," Biswas said. "Our research highlights the importance of understanding the influence of digital devices on our decision-making."
Detailed Research Methodology

Through six studies at various restaurants and two in a USF School of Marketing and Innovation lab, Biswas and his graduate students examined the effects of ordering from a digital menu versus a physical menu. The team reviewed more than 23,000 orders from diverse dining establishments, including an independently owned Mexican cuisine restaurant and a global dining chain with 1,000 locations across 23 countries.
Notable Findings and Food Categorization

The study revealed that 61% of digital orders, including those made for delivery, were unhealthy, more than 3% higher than non-digital orders. Each item was categorized as unhealthy, neutral, or healthy. Unhealthy items consisted of large portions and choices like fried foods and desserts, while items like vegetables and fish were considered healthy. Most soups, large salads, and steaks smaller than six ounces were deemed neutral.

The research also found that digital menus have a greater impact on dinner orders, as consumers tend to be more exhausted and reliant on technology later in the day. Therefore, digital ordering technologies may influence breakfast and lunch choices to a lesser extent.

"Digital ordering modes foster a more automatic decision-making process with lower cognitive involvement,” Biswas noted. “This is because digital tools encourage people to rely less on their cognitive resources and more on automated processes.”
The “Google Effect” and Consumer Proficiency

This phenomenon, known as the "Google Effect," suggests that the availability of digital tools alters how people store and retrieve information. This reduced cognitive involvement in digital contexts can lead to more automatic decision-making, resulting in more indulgent food choices. The study revealed that consumers proficient with technology might be less affected by this phenomenon.
Implications for Restaurant Managers

"Restaurant managers aiming to promote healthier options may benefit from offering non-digital ordering modes, or some may be interested in promoting indulgent items during dinner hours through digital ordering to drive sales," said Biswas.
Future Research Directions

Biswas plans to continue this research to further examine how the presence of a human, such as when ordering in person or on the phone, may impact consumers' decisions. He also aims to investigate how digital versus non-digital modes affect a consumer's consumption volume and perceived taste of ordered items.
